neighbours.label: Tie or impasse between evenly matched sides: ' dead' (-locked, heat), ' stale' (-mate), ' break' (a tie), ' evenly' (split); the same words in other senses stay quiet
fire: After three weeks of bargaining, the two parties were still deadlocked over wages.
The speaker of the assembly may vote only to break a tie.
Polls show the two candidates in a dead heat one week before the election.
The war on the western front settled into a long stalemate.
With the senate deadlocked, the budget could not be passed.
A penalty shootout was needed to break the tie after extra time.
The committee was evenly divided between supporters and opponents of the plan.
Negotiations over the border reached a stalemate last spring.
quiet: After three weeks of bargaining, the two parties finally agreed on wages.
The speaker of the assembly may vote only after a full debate.
Polls show the flowers in the garden were dead one week after the frost.
The crackers on the western shelf had gone stale and soft.
With the senate in recess, the budget could not be passed.
A short rest was needed to break the journey after the long climb.
The butter was evenly spread over both slices of the toast.
Negotiations over the border reached a happy conclusion last spring.

notes: Card: ' dead' x6, ' stale' x6, ' break' x3, ' evenly' x2, all in deadlock/tie contexts; logits promote ' dead', ' deadlock'. Probes: deadlocked 0.65, break a tie 0.56, stalemate 0.27, evenly split 0.24; dead battery 0.002, stale bread 0.001, break the window 0.17.
